lesson: SIZE FIRST, THEN THE NAME LIST - I built the allocation backwards and Adam corrected it twice. I drafted tranches for four names before establishing the pool, assumed 400 PER NAME (1,600), and then had to cut it to two names on a single buy when the real number came back as 400 per kid. The screen work was right; the sequencing was not. ASK FOR THE POOL SIZE BEFORE DRAFTING ANY ACCUMULATION STRUCTURE - the pool determines the name count, the tranche count, and whether tranching is appropriate at all, and none of those can be fixed by editing a plan afterwards. THE SIZE-DEPENDENT RULES THAT FELL OUT OF IT, worth keeping: (1) Under ~500 per position, do not tranche - the entry tick is noise on a long horizon and the admin is real. (2) Under ~1,000 per account, two names beats four - a position that cannot move the account is not diversification. (3) In a DRIP account at small size, YIELD outranks business quality in the ranking, because it is the only compounding mechanism actually operating. GOOGL is the better company than both picks and still came out third on those grounds.

VENUE (decided, Adam 2026-08-15): the kids' money moves to ROBINHOOD CUSTODIAL UTMA, one account per kid, migrating this afternoon. Adam independently confirmed availability; verified against Robinhood's docs - custodial UTMA launched March 2026 and supports stocks, ETFs, recurring investments, RECURRING DEPOSITS, DIVIDEND REINVESTMENT (DRIP) and high-yield cash. TAKE SELF-DIRECTED, not the managed Robinhood Strategies option - there is no reason to pay an advisory percentage on $400 to hold two stocks for fifteen years. WHY IT LEFT GREENLIGHT: Investing for Kids requires Greenlight Max at 10.98/mo = 131.76/yr, which is 3.2x the ~41.20 of annual dividends on the $800 and 16.5% of account value per year; Greenlight's help centre does not document dividend reinvestment at all. Robinhood custodial is free and DRIPs natively. COMPOSITION IS NOW OPEN, AND THIS IS A CORRECTION TO MY OWN B-111 RANKING. Adam asked whether the names were picked only for the dividends. Partly, and yield did more work than it deserved. NKE's dividend is INCIDENTAL - the thesis is gross margin +8.9 pts, net income 5x, and four insiders buying 2.73M above the current price. VICI's yield genuinely IS the return mechanism because a REIT must distribute most of its taxable income, and the real thesis is that it is cheap (PE 10.2, P/B 1.00) with the 6.28% a symptom of that. But letting yield be the TIEBREAKER knocked GOOGL out for the wrong reason: a dividend is not free money (price drops by it on the ex-date), total return is what matters over 15 years, and a 0.25% yielder compounding at 10% on price beats a 6.28% yielder compounding at 7%. The secondary argument - that DRIP buys more shares on down days - largely evaporates once recurring monthly deposits are running, which they should be. THREE OPTIONS ON THE TABLE, ADAM'S CALL, NONE RECORDED AS CHOSEN: (1) GOOGL $200 + VICI $200 - my recommendation, a quality compounder at 17x paired with contractual income at book; (2) keep NKE $200 + VICI $200 and add GOOGL on the next contribution - the B-111 plan, defensible because NKE's insider buying is the most concrete and most current signal of the three; (3) all three at ~$133 - the "too many names" objection was about admin, not math, and three is manageable. GOOGL's fair counter-risk, stated: whether AI erodes search is the live 15-year question for that company and it is unresolved (B-102/B-048). NKE's fair counter-risk: revenue is still declining and a turnaround is a TRADE thesis placed on a HOLD horizon - the highest-variance of the three. UNCHANGED REGARDLESS OF WHICH OPTION WINS: 400 per kid / 800 total, single buy per name, NO tranching at this size, DRIP toggled ON IN EACH ACCOUNT SEPARATELY, a small recurring deposit per account, no price stops (thesis-review markers only).
lesson: CAUGHT BY ADAM, AND IT IS THE SECOND TIME THIS SESSION A ONE-LINE QUESTION EXPOSED A REAL WEAKNESS (the first was the ASPI insider chart). 'Are you only adding these for the dividends?' was correct: I built a ranking where yield was the deciding criterion rather than one input, and it demoted the best business on the list. THE RULE WORTH KEEPING: in a long-horizon hold account, rank on TOTAL RETURN and on business durability. Yield is one component of total return, not a proxy for it, and it is only a genuine tiebreaker when the two candidates are otherwise close AND no new contributions are coming in. Recurring deposits supply the same dollar-cost-averaging benefit that reinvested dividends do, so once a monthly contribution exists the yield argument gets materially weaker. PROCESS NOTE: B-111 was written as a settled plan and is now amended before any money moved, which is the B-073 amendment rule working as intended - a drafted plan is not a decision, and a plan the framework has since argued against must not sit in the book looking settled.
